epics.title: rt suggest — LLM-friendly command discovery and cross-linking
epics.description: Make the rt command catalog queryable by natural-language task. Adds a flat top-level rt suggest <task> meta-command (BM25 + hand-curated synonyms + JSON/text output), a SeeAlso field on RtCommandInfo for inverse/workflow/sibling cross-links, and reuses the same BM25 engine to fix unknown-command parse errors with 'did you mean' suggestions. Purely additive — no command moves or renames.

epics.title: Complete thin-host-adapter migration
epics.description: Apply the Core-service + thin-host-adapter pattern (established in the suggest + outline POC, docs/pattern-core-service.md) to every command. Today most commands route through CliCommandBridge text-capture for MCP, losing structure and forcing dry-run-always for mutations. The POC proved the pattern works; this epic finishes the rollout, drops the unusual RoslynTools.Mcp → RoslynTools.Cli exec-to-exec project reference, and locks the pattern with an architectural ratchet test.
epics.notes: POC learnings to carry into each migration: (1) For commands already ctor-injected post-US-072 (e.g. OutlineCommand), the CLI side needs minimal change - consolidate parameters into a Request DTO. (2) Native MCP handlers return ToolResult{content=JSON} directly; do not route through CapturingConsole. (3) ICommandCatalog abstraction (Core) lets the service stay host-agnostic. (4) Asymmetries are acceptable: CLI has --json/--yaml/--markdown formatting; MCP always returns native JSON; CLI shows progress on stderr, MCP doesn't. Document any new asymmetry in pattern-core-service.md. (5) Mutating commands (refactor/*) raise a design question: MCP currently force-dry-runs them via CliCommandBridge; native handlers need an explicit decision (carve-out or design). US-098 in this epic owns that decision.

epics.title: Command consistency consolidation — checklist becomes compiler-enforced
epics.description: Roll up the strategic outcome that ties EP-007 (JSON output), EP-009 (consistent contracts), EP-011 (suggest discovery), and EP-012 (thin-host-adapter migration) into one coherent landing: interfaces enforce category and capability; the per-command checklist shrinks to genuinely-human items; native MCP handlers replace the auto-bridge for inspect/analyze and follow current MCP spec (structuredContent, outputSchema); every command — including mutating — flows through a shared output-format renderer.
epics.notes:
P1 strategic outcome epic. Owns no stories directly — references stories under EP-007, EP-009, EP-011, and EP-012 in a phased sequencing plan. See docs/consistency-roadmap.md for the full plan with rationale per phase.

Outcome: roughly half the universal per-command checklist becomes compiler- or architecture-test-enforced; the per-command pending-work matrix collapses to genuinely-human items; MCP callers get typed responses with declared output schemas; CLI callers get format consistency across all commands.

Sequencing (high level):
  Phase 1 Foundation (parallel): US-100 (renderer consolidation), US-107 (category + capability interfaces)
  Phase 2 Apply foundation (parallel after phase 1): US-108 (delete Info.Category/Mutates), US-109 (format pipeline to all commands), US-097 (decide refactor MCP shape — design decision)
  Phase 3 MCP modernisation: US-110 (structuredContent + outputSchema), then US-094 (architectural ratchet test)
  Phase 4 Native MCP handler rollout (parallel after phase 3): US-095 inspect, US-096 analyze, US-104 change-signature, US-105 move, US-106 suggest naming
  Phase 5 Project structure (independent track): US-099 extract IRtCommand registry, then US-098 drop Mcp→Cli reference
  Phase 6 Universal metadata (any time, ratcheted): US-084, US-085, US-086, US-088, US-089, US-093, US-103

Done definition: every story listed above is closed AND the architectural ratchet test (US-094) is green AND docs/per-command-checklist.md has been shrunk to the genuinely-human items only.

userStories.title: Introduce SymbolQuery for consistent symbol resolution
userStories.description: As an rt user, I want commands that accept symbols to resolve names, fully qualified names, and ambiguity in the same way across inspect and refactor workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: SymbolQuery is a record in src/RoslynTools/Core/Symbols/SymbolQuery.cs with fields: RawInput (string), ExpectedKind (SymbolKindFilter? — Class/Method/Property/Field/Namespace/Any), Scope (ScopeFilter? — Solution/Project/Namespace path), AmbiguityPolicy (FailOnAmbiguous | PickFirst | PromptViaDecisions).

SymbolResolver (a new service or extension to SymbolLocator) consumes SymbolQuery and returns Result<ISymbol, RtError>: matches exact short names, fully qualified names, and partial dotted paths against the loaded solution.

Exact match: input "WorkspaceLoader" finds the single type named WorkspaceLoader; FQN match: input "RoslynTools.Core.WorkspaceLoader" finds the same; partial match: input "Core.WorkspaceLoader" finds it if no ambiguity in the loaded solution.
Ambiguous matches: when N matches exist and AmbiguityPolicy is FailOnAmbiguous, return RtError.AmbiguousMatch with Context["candidates"] listing each candidate FQN.
No match: return RtError.NotFound with the query input in Context["query"].
Kind mismatch: input matches a symbol whose kind doesn't satisfy ExpectedKind — return RtError.NotFound with Context["foundKind"] set so the caller can produce a precise error message.

At least two existing commands are migrated to consume SymbolQuery: one read-only (e.g. DescribeCommand or FindRefsCommand) and one refactor (e.g. RenameCommand). The migrated commands stop hand-rolling FQN parsing.

AmbiguityPolicy.PromptViaDecisions integrates with the existing DecisionStore: when set, an ambiguous match writes pending entries to the decisions YAML and returns RtError.AmbiguousMatch (caller maps to exit code 2).

Tests cover: exact match, FQN match, partial match success, partial match ambiguous (returns AmbiguousMatch), no match (returns NotFound), kind mismatch (returns NotFound with foundKind), each AmbiguityPolicy branch.
dotnet build clean; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean; existing tests pass; new SymbolResolver tests green.

Pipe-chain smoke: rt inspect find-refs --symbol WorkspaceLoader --json | rt refactor rename --new-name SolutionLoader --dry-run works end-to-end (the FQN-via-stdin from US-056 + SymbolQuery resolution from this story compose cleanly).

dotnet build, dotnet format --verify-no-changes, and the full test suite all clean
userStories.resolution: Completed on branch us-072-ctor-injection (PR forthcoming). IRtCommand.Build() is now an instance member; all ~50 commands under src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ migrated to constructor-injected services (commits 199eefe through e1560db). Three production services (FixNamespaceService, ExtractClassService, ConsoleLoggingCore) also migrated. Bootstrap.cs registers ILogger<> via RtConsoleLogger<> as an open generic so Scrutor-discovered services with ILogger<T> ctor params resolve cleanly. Interface generation: the converted class declares `: I<TypeName>` in its base list with correct whitespace and brace placement (no `IDisposable\n,IFoo{` style malformations).

userStories.title: Standardize CLI options through CommandOptionFactory with consistent vocabulary and aliases
userStories.description: As an rt user, I want common CLI options (--solution, --symbol, --file, --dry-run, --json, --decisions, --threshold, --top, --sort) to be constructed by shared factories so option names, descriptions, defaults, and aliases stay consistent across commands. The factory naming and the vocabulary decision are inseparable: every factory method commits to one canonical option name, so the vocabulary standardisation IS the factory work.
acceptanceCriteria: CommandOptionFactory in src/RoslynTools/Cli/ defines static factory methods for every option that appears in 2+ commands: CreateSolutionOption(), CreateSymbolOption(), CreateFqnOption(), CreateFileOption(), CreateDryRunOption(), CreateJsonOption(), CreateDecisionsOption(), CreateThresholdOption(), CreateTopOption(), CreateSortOption().

Each factory method returns a fully-configured System.CommandLine.Option<T> with: consistent name, consistent description text, consistent default, and any required Alias[] (e.g. --solution accepts -s alias everywhere or nowhere — pick one and apply).

Vocabulary contract: option names are standardised across commands — e.g. --symbol means 'symbol name or FQN to operate on' everywhere it appears; --file means 'a single source file path' everywhere it appears; --top means 'limit output to N entries after sorting' everywhere it appears. Mismatches in existing commands are fixed (with backwards-compatibility aliases for the old names if Dan flags any breaking changes).

All commands that previously hand-rolled these options are migrated to use the factory. Mechanical change — easy to verify via grep that `new Option<string>("--solution"` returns zero hits in src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ after migration.
Architecture test enforces: any new Option<T> declared directly inside a Build() method (not via the factory) for one of the factory-owned names fails the build.
Help text for migrated commands is unchanged in behaviour but the wording is now consistent across the catalog (e.g. --solution help reads the same in every command's --help).

Aliases: where two commands had different aliases for the same conceptual flag (e.g. --sln vs --solution-path), the factory picks one canonical and reuses; the discarded alias either becomes a deprecation alias or is removed if no usage exists.
rt dump-help output reflects the unified option vocabulary; docs/COMMANDS.md regenerates with consistent option descriptions across all commands.

Smoke: 10 sampled commands from inspect/analyze/refactor exercised via dotnet run still parse the same arg strings they accepted before (regression test array of (command, args) tuples).

userStories.title: rt suggest <task>: BM25 scorer + synonym map + JSON/text output
userStories.description: As an LLM agent, I want a flat top-level rt suggest <task> command that returns the most likely rt commands for a natural-language task description, so I can map intent to command name without scanning the full help page. BM25 + hand-curated synonyms over Name/WhenToUse/Examples — no embeddings, no LLM-at-runtime, no external deps. JSON-by-default when piped (per CLAUDE.md convention).
acceptanceCriteria: New top-level meta-command rt suggest <task> wired into App.RunCoreAsync next to DumpHelpCommand.Build() — not registered as IRtCommand, does not appear under inspect/analyze/refactor groups.

Implementation lives in src/RoslynTools.Cli/Suggest/: SuggestCommand.cs (Build() returns a Command), Bm25Scorer.cs (pure function: IReadOnlyList<RtCommandInfo>, string query, int top → IReadOnlyList<SuggestResult>), Synonyms.cs (static readonly map of command-name → string[] synonyms).
Bm25Scorer scores each command against the tokenised query across three fields: Name (and its synonyms) at weight 3.0×, WhenToUse at weight 1.0×, Examples (joined) at weight 0.3×.
Tokenisation: split on whitespace + punctuation, lowercase, drop a small fixed stopword set {a, an, the, is, of, to, in, for, this, that, all}.
BM25 length normalisation prevents a long WhenToUse with one match from dominating a short WhenToUse with one match; k1 and b parameters use standard defaults (k1=1.2, b=0.75).
Output flags: --top N (default 3), --json (explicit override).
Text mode (default at TTY): numbered list, each entry shows name + score + first line of WhenToUse + one example. Colour the name (reuse DumpHelpCommand colour helpers).
JSON mode (--json or stdout not a TTY): array of { name, score, category, whenToUse, example, allExamples }. Designed for LLM ingestion.
Default behaviour: when stdout is not a TTY, emit JSON (matches CLAUDE.md 'read-only inspection commands: JSON to stdout' convention). --json flag forces JSON regardless.
Exit code: 0 always — empty results are a valid answer (a JSON empty array). No exit-1 / exit-2 paths in this command.

Synonym map seed: ~10 high-traffic mismatches — safe-delete←{delete,remove}, replace-datetime←{datetime,utcnow,timeprovider}, convert-static-class←{destatic,to instance,instance class}, convert-to-record←{record,to record}, make-async←{async,task}, extract-method←{extract block,pull out method}, find-callers←{callers,who calls}, find-refs←{references,uses of,usages}, outline←{list members,type members}, describe←{type shape,interface members}. Per-command lists, not free-form.

Theory test tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/SuggestCommandTests.cs pins (query, expected-top-result) pairs: ('extract a method from a block','extract-method'), ('remove DateTime.UtcNow','replace-datetime'), ('convert static class to instance','convert-static-class'), ('find callers of a method','find-callers'), ('rename a symbol','rename'). Tests resolve commands from RoslynTools.Bootstrap.RegisterServices per the feedback_test_di_resolution memory.

BM25 unit tests tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/Bm25ScorerTests.cs cover: single-match-name-wins, WhenToUse-stronger-than-Examples weighting, no-match-returns-empty, length-normalisation-prevents-long-text-dominance.

Documentation: skills/use-rt/SKILL.md gains a one-paragraph 'If you don't know the command name, run rt suggest "<task>" first' pointer; CLAUDE.md → Commands section gains the line 'Don\'t know the name? rt suggest "<task>"'.

userStories.title: Unknown-command fallback: reuse Bm25Scorer to suggest matches on parse errors
userStories.description: As an LLM agent typing a hallucinated or semantically-correct-but-wrong command name (rt destatic-class, rt rm-method, rt rename-symbol), I want rt to suggest the closest real command via the same BM25 engine that powers rt suggest, so I can recover without reading the full help page. System.CommandLine middleware that runs after parse-error detection.
acceptanceCriteria: System.CommandLine middleware registered in App.RunCoreAsync near the existing exception handler runs AFTER parsing and detects 'unknown command' parse errors at the root or group level.

When an unknown token is detected at a top-level or group context, the middleware: (a) emits a single 'Error: <token> is not a recognised command.' line to stderr; (b) runs Bm25Scorer.Score(App.Commands.Select(c => c.Info).ToList(), unknownToken, top: 3) to get ranked candidates; (c) if any candidate scores above a configurable threshold, prints 'Did you mean one of these?' followed by each candidate's name + first-line WhenToUse; (d) prints 'Or run: rt suggest "<task in plain English>"' as a recovery hint; (e) sets context.ExitCode = 1.

When no candidate scores above the threshold (gibberish input), the 'Did you mean' block is suppressed — only the 'is not a recognised command' line + 'Or run: rt suggest ...' hint appears. Printing low-confidence suggestions for gibberish is worse than printing nothing.
Threshold lives in Bm25Scorer as a tunable constant (e.g. MinSuggestionScore); tests pin the threshold by exercising the gibberish case.
The pure-function Bm25Scorer is shared with the rt suggest command (Story 1) — the middleware is just another caller of the same engine; the seeded synonyms apply automatically.
Output channel: stderr per CLAUDE.md 'diagnostics to stderr' convention. Exit code 1 consistent with other user-error exits.
JSON mode honour: if --json was parsed cleanly before the parse error, the 'Did you mean' block is JSON; otherwise plain text.

Theory test tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/UnknownCommandFallbackTests.cs pins (typed-token, expected-top-result) pairs: ('destatic-class','convert-static-class'), ('rm-method','inline-method' or 'safe-delete' depending on tuning), ('rename-symbol','rename'), ('seal','make-sealed'), ('blah',null /*gibberish — no high-scoring suggestion*/).
Existing System.CommandLine UseTypoCorrections() still works for short-Levenshtein typos; this middleware is the layer above for semantic matches that Levenshtein won't catch.
Backwards-compat: invocations that already succeed (every existing command) are unchanged; no measurable startup overhead from the middleware on the happy path (BM25 only runs on parse failure).

userStories.title: Stable fix IDs in dry-run + --apply / --skip filters for batch mutation commands
userStories.description: As an LLM agent or interactive user reviewing a batch rt refactor --dry-run, I want each proposed fix labelled with a stable deterministic ID, and I want to re-invoke the command with --apply <ids,...> or --skip <ids,...> to land exactly the subset I've decided is safe. Without this, accepting 5 of 8 proposed make-sealed changes requires hand-editing or splitting the batch by symbol name.
acceptanceCriteria: Every fix proposed by a batch mutation command (make-sealed, add-null-checks, add-global-import, convert-console-logging, replace-xunit-asserts, replace-datetime, add-xml-doc) is tagged with an 8-char hex fix ID derived from SHA-256 over (commandName + targetSymbolFqnOrRepoRelativePath + mutationKind); the ID is deterministic across runs as long as the inputs haven't changed.
When the target has no FQN (file-scoped operations), the hash falls back to repo-relative path + mutation kind — stable across runs as long as the file isn't moved/renamed.
Dry-run text output prefixes each diff section with `[fix <id>]` on its own line above the `--- path` header so the ID is grep-pable.
Dry-run JSON output (for commands that already emit JSON, or as a follow-up for those that don't) wraps each fix in `{ id, command, target, files: [{ path, diff }] }`.
A `--apply <id,id,...>` option, when present, narrows the applied set to fixes whose ID is in the list; unknown IDs are reported to stderr and exit 1.
A `--skip <id,id,...>` option, when present, applies all fixes except those listed; unknown IDs are reported to stderr and exit 1.
Passing both --apply and --skip in the same invocation is a usage error: exit 1 with a clear stderr message.
Neither --apply nor --skip require --dry-run to have been run first; IDs are deterministic so the user can compute them once and pass them later.
When --apply selects zero fixes (empty list or all IDs unknown), the command exits 0 with `No changes.` (existing no-op message) rather than failing.

Single-target commands (rename, move, extract-method, inline-method, safe-delete) emit a single fix ID in their dry-run header for consistency, but --apply/--skip are *not* registered on them (no benefit and adds parse-time noise).

Integration tests under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Mutation/ cover: (a) determinism — same input twice produces same ID; (b) --apply picks subset; (c) --skip drops subset; (d) both flags error; (e) unknown ID errors; (f) ID stability across an unrelated edit elsewhere in the project.

userStories.notes: P2. Centralise ID generation in a new FixId helper in src/RoslynTools/Core/. Each batch command's service exposes the candidate fix list (already does internally — just needs to lift it before SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync) so the command host can apply --apply/--skip filtering before workspace changes are computed. Option registration: extend CommandOptionFactory with CreateApplyOption()/CreateSkipOption() and a shared parser. Scope: batch commands only (single-target commands gain nothing from --apply/--skip). Out of scope for MVP: backporting --apply/--skip to single-target commands; JSON envelope for commands that today emit only text diffs (track as a follow-up under EP-007 if useful).

userStories.title: Delete redundant RtCommandInfo.Category and Info.Mutates after category interfaces land
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a single source of truth for a command's category and mutation behaviour: the interface it implements. Today Info.Category and Info.Mutates duplicate that signal and will drift after US-107 introduces category and capability interfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: RtCommandInfo no longer carries a string Category field. The category is determined exclusively by which marker interface (IInspectCommand/IAnalyzeCommand/IRefactorCommand) the command implements.

RtCommandInfo no longer carries a bool Mutates field. Whether a command mutates is determined exclusively by whether it implements IMutatingCommand (or by being an IRefactorCommand — pick one canonical rule and document it).

All callers that previously read Info.Category — including DumpHelpCommand, App.RunAsync startup check, ToolSchemaBuilder, and rt suggest scoring — now read the category from the interface via a single helper (e.g. CategoryOf(IRtCommand) returning a `Category` enum)
All callers that previously read Info.Mutates — including ToolSchemaBuilder, DumpHelpCommand, the MCP auto-bridge — now read it from the interface check

If Info.Category / Info.Mutates can not be cleanly deleted in one pass (e.g. external scripts depend on the dump-help JSON shape), they are kept as read-only computed properties derived from the interface and the derivation is the single source of truth — no setter, no constructor parameter

MCP host always serves the JSON form regardless of CLI --format (MCP is a structured protocol); the CLI --format flag is purely a terminal-rendering choice

userStories.title: Modernise MCP result shape: structuredContent, outputSchema, typed content array
userStories.description: As an MCP client (LLM agent), I want native handler responses to follow current MCP best practices — typed content[] array, structuredContent for typed responses, outputSchema declared in tools/list — so I can validate response shape, avoid double-JSON-parsing, and rely on the protocol's typed result contract. Today ToolResult flattens the entire JSON response into a single content string.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit the current MCP wire format produced by Server.HandleCallToolAsync against the MCP CallToolResult schema. Document any divergence (e.g. content returned as a single string vs. as a content[] array of typed items).

Server returns CallToolResult with a typed content array: {content: [{type: "text", text: "..."}], isError: bool}. Today our ToolResult(bool isError, string content) flattens the structured result into a single text item — if that is already happening server-side, document it; if not, fix it

Evaluate upgrading the MCP protocolVersion declared in HandleInitialize (currently "2024-11-05") to a revision that supports structuredContent and outputSchema (e.g. "2025-06-18" or later). Decision recorded in docs/pattern-core-service.md.
If upgrading: tools/list entries declare outputSchema alongside inputSchema for every native IMcpHandler. The outputSchema describes the response shape so callers can validate and type-check.

If upgrading: tools/call responses include structuredContent (the typed object) alongside a text fallback in content[] for legacy clients. The native handler stops serialising to JSON-string and instead returns the typed object directly through a new ToolResult shape (e.g. ToolResult.Structured(object) / ToolResult.Error(string)).

If NOT upgrading (decision documented): at minimum verify the existing 2024-11-05 wire format is correct — content[] array of typed items, isError flag, error responses use isError=true not JSON-RPC error.

Every native handler (Outline, Suggest, FindRefs, Rename, plus the EP-012 backlog) emits the modernised result shape. Tests under tests/RoslynTools.Tests.Mcp/ assert the wire format against the schema.

MCP best-practice checklist added as a section of docs/pattern-core-service.md or docs/per-command-checklist.md: ToolName naming convention, required-field declaration, structuredContent + outputSchema usage, error vs success conventions, content[] vs structuredContent guidance, when to set isError=true

Pattern reference: commit 6d767b1 (feat(mcp): wire find_refs and rename as native MCP handlers). The new ToolResult shape and any protocol-version uplift propagates to those handlers and to OutlineHandler / SuggestHandler.
Composes with US-094 (the MCP-handler ratchet test should also assert outputSchema is declared for every native handler if the protocol-version uplift lands)

userStories.title: rt refactor add-base-type: add interface or base class to a class declaration without generating stubs
userStories.description: As an rt user applying empty marker interfaces (US-107 introduces 6), I want a one-shot command that adds an interface to a class's base list across many classes at once, without rt refactor implement-interface's stub generation. Today I have to fall back to manual Edit on every file, which defeats the whole point of dogfooding rt for mechanical refactors.
acceptanceCriteria: rt has a new command `rt refactor add-base-type` (or equivalent --no-stubs flag on existing implement-interface) that adds an interface or base class to a target class declaration's base list without generating member stubs.

Use case: empty marker interfaces (e.g. IInspectCommand, IAnalyzeCommand, IRefactorCommand, IMutatingCommand). Today rt refactor implement-interface generates throw-stubs, which is wrong for empty markers.

Supports targeting all classes matching a filter in one invocation: `rt refactor add-base-type --in-namespace RoslynTools.Commands --where 'Info.Category == "inspect"' --add-interface IInspectCommand --solution RoslynTools.slnx` or a similar shape. Mechanical bulk application is the primary motivation.
Single-target mode: `rt refactor add-base-type --class RoslynTools.Commands.RenameCommand --add-interface IRefactorCommand --solution RoslynTools.slnx`
Standard rt conventions: --dry-run, --solution auto-detect, stderr diagnostics, structured JSON output reporting which classes were modified
Surfaced during US-107 planning (2026-05-25). FB reference: planner had to fall back to manual Edit on ~52 command classes for Batches 2 and 3 of US-107.
Pattern reference: rt refactor implement-interface (similar surface, but emits stubs)
